methodology_note: Study units derived from Toronto Notes SOURCE STRUCTURE (toc_inventory.json / derived/scope_packets/GM.json). Chapter GM has 27 source nodes, 0 unresolved headings, and is HIGH confidence at the section (level-2) tier; its 17 level-3 topic nodes are all TOC_OCR_UNANCHORED (LOW confidence, meaning per-topic page anchoring was not independently confirmed though the topic titles themselves are unmerged and unambiguous). GM.S01 carries a merged_duplicate_headings record ('Physiology and Pathology of Aging') alongside its printed title 'ACFOMYMS' (an OCR-corrupted mnemonic acronym); the merged heading is used as the study-unit title since it is legible and unambiguous, per the rule against inventing headings but in favour of using a source-confirmed alternate label over a garbled one. GM.S05 similarly carries a merged heading ('Healthcare Institutions') alongside its printed title 'Hazards of Hospitalization'; both are combined in the unit title since neither is clearly the single canonical heading. GM.S09's printed title 'RETEFEMCES' is an unambiguous OCR corruption of 'REFERENCES' (consistent with the chapter's terminal bibliography position, mirroring the References leaf section seen in every other completed chapter) and is represented under its corrected reading. GM.S03 ('Presentations in Older Adults') is a genuine umbrella of 11 distinct geriatric syndromes (Constipation, Delirium, Elder Abuse, Falls, Frailty, Immobility, Incontinence, Malnutrition, Presbycusis, Presbyopia, Pressure Injuries) each carrying independent clinical content and, in most cases, independent MCC evidence - per the geriatrics scope principle that broad syndromes may warrant distinct units where source content supports it, no consolidation was applied here. GM.S04 ('Driving Competency', T01 Reporting Requirements + T02 Conditions That May Impair Driving) and GM.S06 ('Geriatric Pharmacology', T01 Pharmacokinetics + T02 Pharmacodynamics + T03 Polypharmacy + T04 Inappropriate Prescribing) were each consolidated into fewer units than T-children: driving's two T-children are two facets of one fitness-to-drive competency; pharmacology's four T-children split naturally into a mechanistic pair (PK/PD, background) and an applied-practice pair (polypharmacy/inappropriate prescribing, the actually-tested content), consistent with not fragmenting generic subheadings absent independent testing evidence for each.

organizational_header_nodes.GM.S03: 'Presentations in Older Adults' umbrella heading (GM4-GM13); carries no independent content beyond its 11 T-children, represented as SU-GM-03 through SU-GM-13 (one study unit per distinct geriatric syndrome, no consolidation).
organizational_header_nodes.GM.S04: 'Driving Competency' umbrella heading (GM14); carries no independent content beyond its two T-children, both represented together as SU-GM-14 (Reporting Requirements + Conditions That May Impair Driving are two facets of one fitness-to-drive competency).
organizational_header_nodes.GM.S06: 'Geriatric Pharmacology' umbrella heading (GM16-GM17); carries no independent content beyond its four T-children, represented as SU-GM-16 (Pharmacokinetics + Pharmacodynamics, mechanistic background) and SU-GM-17 (Polypharmacy + Inappropriate Prescribing, applied/tested content).

study_units.title: Physiology and Pathology of Aging
study_units.structural_rationale: Level-2 section (HIGH confidence, TOC_OCR) with no T-children; printed title is 'ACFOMYMS' (an OCR-corrupted mnemonic acronym), but merged_duplicate_headings records the legible alternate title 'Physiology and Pathology of Aging', used here per the rule favouring a source-confirmed legible label over an unreadable one. Covers normal age-related organ-system changes underlying the disease-specific units that follow.

study_units.title: Framework for the Approach to the Older Adult (Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment)
study_units.structural_rationale: Level-2 section (HIGH confidence, TOC_OCR) with no T-children; TOC heading 'Framework for the Approach to the Older Adult'. Covers the multidimensional/functional assessment approach (function, cognition, mobility, social supports) that structures the syndrome-specific units that follow. Clinical cognitive/functional assessment is kept distinct here from legal decision-making capacity, consent, and substitute decision-making, which remain ELOM territory pending global ownership resolution.

study_units.title: Constipation in Older Adults
study_units.structural_rationale: TOC heading 'Constipation', a T-child (LOW confidence, TOC_OCR_UNANCHORED) of the 'Presentations in Older Adults' umbrella section. Chapter G's SU-G-25 already covers adult constipation generally; this unit's distinct content is age-related contributing factors (polypharmacy, immobility, low fluid/fibre intake, cognitive impairment affecting recognition/reporting).

study_units.title: Delirium
study_units.structural_rationale: TOC heading 'Delirium', a T-child (LOW confidence, TOC_OCR_UNANCHORED) of the 'Presentations in Older Adults' umbrella section. A core geriatric-syndrome unit; includes distinguishing delirium from dementia (the older adult's high baseline prevalence of underlying neurocognitive disorder is the central diagnostic challenge). Overlaps Psychiatry and Neurology, which may cover delirium's psychiatric/neurologic mechanism in more depth.

study_units.title: Driving Competency in Older Adults
study_units.structural_rationale: TOC headings 'Reporting Requirements' and 'Conditions That May Impair Driving' are two unmerged T-children (LOW confidence, TOC_OCR_UNANCHORED) of the 'Driving Competency' umbrella section, consolidated into one unit as two facets of a single fitness-to-drive competency (what conditions impair driving, and the physician's reporting obligation). Physician mandatory-reporting rules for medically unfit drivers are provincial/territorial in Canada; retained as jurisdiction-sensitive content pending future verification rather than treated as a Canada-wide rule.

study_units.title: Hazards of Hospitalization (Healthcare Institutions)
study_units.structural_rationale: Level-2 section (HIGH confidence, TOC_OCR) with no T-children; printed title 'Hazards of Hospitalization', merged_duplicate_headings additionally records 'Healthcare Institutions'. Covers iatrogenic/institutional risks specific to hospitalized older adults (deconditioning, delirium precipitation, nosocomial infection, functional decline) and the range of care settings (acute care, rehabilitation, long-term care).
